facts.statement: Argovisaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurian ichthyosaurs that lived in the Middle Jurassic of Switzerland.
facts.quote: Argovisaurus (meaning "Aargau lizard") is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurian ichthyosaurs from the Middle Jurassic (Bajocian) Hauptrogenstein Formation of Switzerland.

facts.statement: The genus Argovisaurus contains only one known species, A. martafernandezi, which is known from a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, A. martafernandezi, known from a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: Argovisaurus was notably large compared to its relatives.
facts.quote: Argovisaurus was a large ichthyosaur compared to its relatives.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered before 2004 by Elmar Meier in the Hauptrogenstein Formation near Auenstein, Switzerland.
facts.quote: The Argovisaurus holotype specimen, PIMUZ A/III 5279, was discovered and collected before 2004 by Elmar Meier in sediments of the Hauptrogenstein Formation near Auenstein in Canton of Aargau, Switzerland.

facts.statement: Miedema et al. formally described Argovisaurus martafernandezi as a new genus and species in 2024.
facts.quote: In 2024, Miedema et al. described Argovisaurus martafernandezi as a new genus and species of ophthalmosaurian ichthyosaur based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The name Argovisaurus combines the Latin name for the region of discovery with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, "Argovisaurus", combines "Argovia", the Latin name of Aargau, where the fossil was discovered, with the Greek "σαῦρος" ("sauros"), meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: The species name honors paleontologist Marta Fernández for her work on marine reptiles.
facts.quote: The specific name, "martafernandezi", honors Marta Fernández and her paleontological work on marine reptiles including ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype individual was estimated to be between 4.5 and 6 meters long.
facts.quote: The holotype individual of Argovisaurus likely belonged to an animal between 4.5 - 6 m long, similar in size to Mollesaurus.

facts.statement: The mandible of the holotype specimen is approximately 125 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The mandible of the Argovisaurus is about 125 cm long.

facts.statement: Several bones in the skull and skeleton show abnormalities that may be evidence of traumatic injuries.
facts.quote: Several of the bones of the skull and skeleton preserve abnormalities that may be attributable to traumatic injuries.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Argovisaurus as an early-diverging member of the Ophthalmosauria.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Miedema et al. (2024) recovered Argovisaurus as an early-diverging member of the Ophthalmosauria.

facts.statement: Although phylogenetic trees place Argovisaurus basal to the strict definition of Ophthalmosauria, authors argue it should be considered a member due to morphological similarities.
facts.quote: The resulting tree placed Argovisaurus in a position basal to the technical definition of the clade Ophthalmosauria, but the authors advocated that it should still be regarded as a member of this clade due to the morphological similarities.

facts.statement: Argovisaurus belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Argovisaurus lived between 170.9 and 165.3 million years ago during the Bajocian to Bathonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bathonian (170.9 to 165.3 million years ago)
